newsitem.title: India: India steps up fight against dengue, death toll 156.
newsitem.headline: India steps up fight against dengue, death toll 156.

text.p: Indian authorities on Tuesday stepped up their campaign against an outbreak of dengue fever in the Indian capital which has already claimed 156 lives.
Delhi Chief Minister Sahib Singh Verma ordered the immediate recruitment of 200 medical officers to cope with the increasing number of dengue-affected patients, officials said.

Hospitals in the capital have been asked to increase the number of beds and have been specifically instructed to not to turn away any patient reporting sick with dengue fever, Vinod Jain, a senior Delhi health official said.
With 11 more deaths reported overnight, at least 156 persons had died in the city and 3,290 were admitted to hospitals with dengue, Jain told Reuters.
But officials said the rate of fatalities appeared to be slowing.
"Even though the number of people reporting sick of dengue fever is quite high, the number of deaths is going down due to their timely arrival (for treatment)," Jain said.
Non-governmental organisations say the actual figures could be much higher as the official death toll does not include casualties in private hospitals.
"What we are seeing is only the tip ot the iceberg as the data available is coming from very limited places," said Pramesh Bhatnagar of the Voluntary Health Association of India.

On Monday, Delhi's Lieutenant-Governor P.K. Dave asked the army to open its hospitals to patients with dengue fever and to deploy units to spray areas of the capital where mosquitoes which carry the disease breed, an aide to Dave said.

Dengue fever, which is also called breakbone fever, erupted in New Delhi in the last week of August during annual monsoon rains. Accompanied by high fever, headaches and pain in muscles and joints, dengue normally runs its course in six to seven days.
But a haemorrhagic form of dengue that can lead to internal bleeding and death has spread in the crowded capital.
Health officials said the epidemic had taken the largest toll in 20 years in any single outbreak in the city.
